Maternity Waiting Shelters and Pregnancy Outcomes in Rural Zimbabwe This study, conducted by JK Ne and PS Dungare, examines the role of maternity waiting shelters in improving pregnancy outcomes in a rural area of Zimbabwe. Published in the Annals of Tropical Paediatrics in 1996, the research highlights the potential benefits of these facilities in reducing maternal and neonatal complications. 2. Community Interventions for Safe Motherhood in Eritrea Turan, Tesfagiorghis, and Polan evaluated a community-based intervention aimed at promoting safe motherhood practices in Eritrea. Their findings, published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health in 2011, emphasize the importance of community engagement in improving maternal health outcomes. 3. Human Rights-Based Approach to Reducing Maternal Mortality A technical guidance document outlines the application of a human rights-based approach to implementing policies and programs designed to reduce preventable maternal morbidity and mortality. This document was accessed on November 26, 2014, and provides a framework for integrating human rights principles into maternal health strategies. 4. Maternal and Perinatal Death Inquiry and Response in India This report discusses the empowerment of communities through maternal and perinatal death inquiries to prevent maternal deaths in India. The document, accessed on November 26, 2014, underscores the role of community participation in addressing maternal mortality. 5. Maternal Care Utilization in Rural Zimbabwe Van den Heuvel et al. conducted a population-based study on the utilization of maternal care services in rural Zimbabwe. Published in Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica in 1999, the study identifies barriers to accessing maternal healthcare in resource-limited settings. 6. Maternity Waiting Homes in Rural Zambia Van Lonkhuijzen and colleagues explored the use of maternity waiting homes in rural Zambia. Their findings, published in the South African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2003, highlight the effectiveness of these facilities in improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. 7. Maternity Waiting Facilities in Low-Resource Countries A systematic review by Van Lonkhuijzen, Stekelenburg, and Van Roosmalen, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2009, evaluates the impact of maternity waiting facilities on maternal and neonatal health in low-resource settings. 8. Involving Men in Maternity Care in India Varkey et al. investigated the involvement of men in maternity care in India. Their report, accessed on January 12, 2015, highlights the positive impact of male participation on maternal and newborn health outcomes. 9. Increasing Skilled Health Personnel in Traditional Birth Settings Vieira et al. conducted a systematic review on strategies to increase the use of skilled health personnel in settings where traditional birth attendants are the primary providers of childbirth care. Published in PLoS ONE in 2012, the study emphasizes the importance of transitioning to skilled care to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. 10. Quality Appraisal of Qualitative Research in Midwifery Walsh and Downe published a critical appraisal of qualitative research methodologies in midwifery in the journal Midwifery in 2006. Their work provides a framework for evaluating the rigor and reliability of qualitative studies in maternal health. 11. Access to Maternity Waiting Homes in Rural Timor-Leste Wild et al. examined the challenges of accessing maternity waiting homes in rural Timor-Leste. Published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2012, the study highlights the impact of geographic and infrastructural barriers on maternal health service utilization. 12. Systematic Review of Maternal Emergency Transport in Low-Income Countries Wilson et al. conducted a systematic review and thematic synthesis of qualitative studies on maternal emergency transport in lowand middle-income countries. Published in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics in 2013, the review identifies key factors influencing the effectiveness of emergency transport systems. 13. The Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion The Ottawa Charter, developed by the World Health Organization in 1986, provides a foundational framework for health promotion, emphasizing the importance of enabling individuals and communities to take control of their health. 14. The Role of Skilled Birth Attendants in Safe Pregnancy A joint statement by WHO, ICM, and FIGO highlights the critical role of skilled birth attendants in ensuring safe pregnancy and childbirth. This document, accessed on January 28, 2015, underscores the need for trained personnel in maternal health services. 15. Maternal Mortality Estimates for 2005 A report by WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, and the World Bank provides global estimates of maternal mortality for 2005. The document, accessed on January 7, 2015, offers insights into the progress and challenges in reducing maternal deaths worldwide. 16. Global Strategy for Women’s and Children’s Health The UN Secretary-General’s global strategy outlines key priorities for improving the health of women and children. This strategy, accessed on January 7, 2015, emphasizes the importance of collaboration and investment in maternal and child health. 17. Improving Maternal and Newborn Health through Community Engagement A WHO publication from 2010 discusses strategies for working with individuals, families, and communities to enhance maternal and newborn health. The document highlights the role of community-based interventions in achieving better health outcomes. 18. WHO Recommendations on Health Promotion for Maternal and Newborn Health This comprehensive guideline, developed by WHO in 2014, provides evidence-based recommendations for health promotion interventions aimed at improving maternal and newborn health outcomes. 19. Tracking Maternal Mortality Declines in Mongolia Yadamsuren et al. analyzed the decline in maternal mortality in Mongolia between 1992 and 2007. Published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2010, the study attributes the progress to effective collaboration and targeted interventions. 20. Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness Programs A systematic review by Solnes Miltenburg et al. evaluates the effectiveness of birth preparedness and complication readiness programs in reducing maternal and neonatal mortality in developing countries. The findings emphasize the importance of planning and readiness in improving health outcomes. 21. Male Involvement in Maternal and Newborn Health Tokhi et al. conducted a systematic review on the role of male involvement in improving maternal and newborn health outcomes. The review highlights the positive impact of engaging men in maternal health initiatives. 22. Cultural Adaptation of Maternity Care Services Coast et al. reviewed interventions aimed at providing culturally appropriate maternity care to increase the uptake of skilled maternity services. Their findings underscore the importance of tailoring healthcare services to meet the cultural needs of diverse populations. 23. Continuous Support During Labor and Birth Hodnett et al. conducted a systematic review on the benefits of continuous support for women during childbirth. Published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2011, the study highlights the positive impact of companionship on maternal and neonatal outcomes. 24. Community Mobilization for Maternal and Newborn Health Prost et al. reviewed the effectiveness of women’s groups practicing participatory learning and action to improve maternal and newborn health in low-resource settings. Published in The Lancet in 2013, the study demonstrates the value of community mobilization in achieving better health outcomes. 25. Community Participation in Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance WHO recommendations emphasize the importance of community participation in analyzing and disseminating information from maternal and perinatal death surveillance systems. This approach aims to improve accountability and prevent future deaths. 26. Community Participation in Quality Improvement Processes WHO highlights the role of community involvement in quality improvement processes for maternal and newborn health services. Engaging communities ensures that healthcare interventions are responsive to local needs. 27. Community Participation in Program Planning and Implementation Marston et al. conducted a systematic review on the effects of community participation in program planning and implementation for maternal and newborn health. The findings underscore the importance of involving communities in decision-making processes to enhance healthcare delivery. These descriptions provide a detailed and professional summary of the references, suitable for a medical expert audience.
